post.summary: BuildOnion attempts to build an onion packet for the specified route.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
BuildOnionRequest includes the necessary information to construct a Sphinx
onion packet.

post.summary:
DeleteAttempts removes terminal (settled or failed) payment attempt records
from the server's attempt store. The client explicitly names the attempt
IDs to delete, enabling online garbage collection of completed attempt
data.
post.description:
The server processes each attempt ID independently and reports per-ID
results. Pending (in-flight) attempts are never deleted; they are reported
with a DELETION_PENDING status. Unknown attempt IDs are reported with
DELETION_NOT_FOUND. Unprocessable records are reported with
DELETION_FAILED. The overall RPC succeeds (gRPC OK) as long as the
request could be processed, even if individual attempts were not deleted.

Clients MUST only delete attempts whose outcome (settled or failed) has
been durably recorded and will never need to be retried. Deleting an
attempt removes the server's idempotency protection for that attempt ID.

post.summary:
DisableRemoteRouter marks the database as no longer being used by a remote
router. This is useful for migrating from a remote router setup back to the
default embedded router. This RPC will fail if there are any attempt entries
remaining in the network result store.

SendOnion dispatches a pre-formed onion packet. It is the primary entry
point for a remote router, and it is idempotent: a client can and should
retry it after a timeout or disconnection, reusing the same attempt_id so
the server recognises the retry rather than sending a second HTLC.
post.description:
The outcome is carried in the response, never in a gRPC error. Exactly one
of Accepted, Rejected or Ambiguous is set, and each documents the action it
obliges the caller to take. An outcome the client does not recognise, or a
response with none set, MUST be treated as Ambiguous.

A gRPC error means the call failed rather than the HTLC: a malformed
request, an auth failure, a transport problem, or a server not running this
sub-server. A client that cannot tell those apart MUST retry the same
attempt_id, because a call that never reached the server and a call whose
response was lost look identical from outside.

A malformed request (InvalidArgument) also records the attempt as failed,
so resend a corrected request under a new attempt_id.

post.summary:
TrackOnion reports the result of an attempt dispatched with SendOnion. Call
it once SendOnion has answered Accepted; resolve any other SendOnion answer
with SendOnion.
post.description:
The answer is carried in the response, never in a gRPC error. At most one
of preimage, failure_details, in_flight or no_record is set, and each
documents the action it obliges the caller to take. A result the client
does not recognise, or a response with none set, means the attempt may
still be live: keep tracking it and never treat it as failed.

By default the call waits until the attempt resolves. With track_mode set
to TRACK_MODE_PEEK it answers at once, reporting an unresolved attempt as
InFlight.

A gRPC error means the call failed rather than describing the attempt: a
malformed request (InvalidArgument), an auth failure, a transport problem,
a passed deadline, an internal error, or a switch shutting down. Retry the
same request, correcting it first if it was malformed.

chan_id.description:
The unique channel ID for the channel. The first 3 bytes are the block
height, the next 3 the index within the block, and the last 2 bytes are the
output index for the channel.

pub_key.description:
An optional public key of the hop. If the public key is given, the payment
can be executed without relying on a copy of the channel graph.

tlv_payload.description:
If set to true, then this hop will be encoded using the new variable length
TLV format. Note that if any custom tlv_records below are specified, then
this field MUST be set to true for them to be encoded properly.

mpp_record.description:
An optional TLV record that signals the use of an MPP payment. If present,
the receiver will enforce that the same mpp_record is included in the final
hop payload of all non-zero payments in the HTLC set. If empty, a regular
single-shot payment is or was attempted.

amp_record.description:
An optional TLV record that signals the use of an AMP payment. If present,
the receiver will treat all received payments including the same
(payment_addr, set_id) pair  as being part of one logical payment. The
payment will be settled by XORing the root_share's together and deriving the
child hashes and preimages according to BOLT XX. Must be used in conjunction
with mpp_record.

custom_records.description:
An optional set of key-value TLV records. This is useful within the context
of the SendToRoute call as it allows callers to specify arbitrary K-V pairs
to drop off at each hop within the onion.

metadata.description: The payment metadata to send along with the payment to the payee.

blinding_point.description:
Blinding point is an optional blinding point included for introduction
nodes in blinded paths. This field is mandatory for hops that represents
the introduction point in a blinded path.

encrypted_data.description:
Encrypted data is a receiver-produced blob of data that provides hops
in a blinded route with forwarding data. As this data is encrypted by
the recipient, we will not be able to parse it - it is essentially an
arbitrary blob of data from our node's perspective. This field is
mandatory for all hops in a blinded path, including the introduction
node.

total_amt_msat.description:
The total amount that is sent to the recipient (possibly across multiple
HTLCs), as specified by the sender when making a payment to a blinded path.
This value is only set in the final hop payload of a blinded payment. This
value is analogous to the MPPRecord that is used for regular (non-blinded)
MPP payments.

payment_addr.description:
A unique, random identifier used to authenticate the sender as the intended
payer of a multi-path payment. The payment_addr must be the same for all
subpayments, and match the payment_addr provided in the receiver's invoice.
The same payment_addr must be used on all subpayments. This is also called
payment secret in specifications (e.g. BOLT 11).

total_amt_msat.description:
The total amount in milli-satoshis being sent as part of a larger multi-path
payment. The caller is responsible for ensuring subpayments to the same node
and payment_hash sum exactly to total_amt_msat. The same
total_amt_msat must be used on all subpayments.

total_time_lock.description:
The cumulative (final) time lock across the entire route. This is the CLTV
value that should be extended to the first hop in the route. All other hops
will decrement the time-lock as advertised, leaving enough time for all
hops to wait for or present the payment preimage to complete the payment.

total_fees.description:
The sum of the fees paid at each hop within the final route. In the case
of a one-hop payment, this value will be zero as we don't need to pay a fee
to ourselves.

total_amt.description:
The total amount of funds required to complete a payment over this route.
This value includes the cumulative fees at each hop. As a result, the HTLC
extended to the first-hop in the route will need to have at least this many
satoshis, otherwise the route will fail at an intermediate node due to an
insufficient amount of fees.

hops.description: Contains details concerning the specific forwarding details at each hop.

first_hop_amount_msat.description:
The actual on-chain amount that was sent out to the first hop. This value is
only different from the total_amt_msat field if this is a custom channel
payment and the value transported in the HTLC is different from the BTC
amount in the HTLC. If this value is zero, then this is an old payment that
didn't have this value yet and can be ignored.

custom_channel_data.description: Custom channel data that might be populated in custom channels.

source_pub_key.description:
The source node from whose perspective the route was built. Defaults to
the node's own public key.

lnrpcRoute.description:
A path through the channel graph which runs over one or more channels in
succession. This struct carries all the information required to craft the
Sphinx onion packet, and send the payment along the first hop in the path. A
route is only selected as valid if all the channels have sufficient capacity to
carry the initial payment amount after fees are accounted for.

already_registered.description:
Set when the switch already held this attempt from an earlier call,
either because the attempt was already registered or because a circuit
for it already existed. Required behaviour is identical either way; this
is diagnostic.

A circuit without a registration should not occur in correct operation.
It means the attempt_id is also in use by another dispatcher, such as
lnd's own router, so the result later tracked may belong to that
dispatcher's HTLC. Keep attempt_ids unique.

switchrpcAccepted.description:
Accepted means the switch has taken ownership of this attempt. Await the
result with TrackOnion.

Do NOT conclude success or failure from this message. It reports who owns
the attempt, not how it ended.

reason.description:
A human-readable reason, for logs and metrics.

Behaviour MUST NOT branch on this value. Every ambiguous outcome
requires the same action, and a caller that treats one reason
differently from another will eventually treat one of them unsafely.
It is free text rather than an enum for exactly that reason.

switchrpcAmbiguous.description:
Ambiguous means the switch cannot determine whether it took ownership of the
attempt.

The caller MUST retry the same attempt_id until it receives Accepted or
Rejected, and MUST NOT record a terminal outcome for the attempt in the
meantime. Retrying is safe: the switch recognises an attempt it already
holds and answers Accepted rather than dispatching a second HTLC.

attempt_id.description: The attempt ID this result corresponds to.

status.description: The outcome of the deletion for this attempt.

switchrpcAttemptDeletionResult.description: AttemptDeletionResult reports the outcome of deleting a single attempt.

switchrpcAttemptDeletionStatus.description:
AttemptDeletionStatus describes the outcome of a single attempt deletion.

 - DELETION_OK: The attempt result was successfully deleted from the store.
 - DELETION_PENDING: The attempt is still in-flight (pending) and cannot be safely deleted.
 - DELETION_NOT_FOUND: The attempt ID was not found in the store. This may indicate a client
bug (wrong ID, wrong backend) since the server has no record of this
attempt ever existing.
 - DELETION_FAILED: The attempt record exists but could not be processed (e.g.
deserialization error). The record remains in the store.

route.description: The route for which the onion packet should be built.

payment_hash.description: The payment hash associated with the HTLC.

session_key.description:
A session key for onion packet construction, if not provided, a new one
will be generated.

switchrpcBuildOnionRequest.description:
BuildOnionRequest includes the necessary information to construct a Sphinx
onion packet.

onion_blob.description: The constructed onion packet in bytes.

session_key.description: The session key used for building the onion packet.

hop_pubkeys.description:
The serialized public keys of all nodes along the route for the
constructed onion.

switchrpcBuildOnionResponse.description: BuildOnionResponse contains the constructed onion packet.

attempt_ids.description:
The attempt IDs to delete from the server's attempt store. Only terminal
(settled or failed) attempts will be deleted. Pending (in-flight)
attempts are skipped and reported with a DELETION_PENDING status.

results.description:
Per-attempt deletion outcomes. The order corresponds to the order of
attempt_ids in the request.

error_message.description: A human-readable error_message for logging or display.

local_failure.description:
local_failure is set when the failure originates at the local
node (e.g. unable to forward due to insufficient balance,
channel policy violations, or other link-level rejections). The
wire message is available in plaintext without onion decryption.

forwarding_failure.description:
forwarding_failure is set when the HTLC was forwarded into the
network and a remote node returned an error. The onion error
was successfully decrypted, yielding the failure source index.
The wire_message may be empty if the inner failure could not
be decoded.

encrypted_error_data.description:
encrypted_error_data contains the raw onion-encrypted error
blob. This is returned when no decryption keys were provided
in the TrackOnionRequest (i.e. no session key or hop public
keys), deferring decryption entirely to the client.

unreadable_failure.description:
unreadable_failure indicates that decryption keys were provided
and decryption was attempted, but failed. The original error
cannot be recovered.

switch_error.description:
switch_error is set when the HTLC failed but the server could
not encode its failure message. The reason is in error_message.

switchrpcFailureDetails.description:
FailureDetails provides structured information about why a payment attempt
failed on the network. This message is included in a successful
TrackOnionResponse when the queried attempt ultimately failed.

failure_source_index.description:
failure_source_index is the 0-based index of the node within the payment
route that reported the failure. Index 0 refers to the local node.

wire_message.description:
The raw, serialized lnwire.FailureMessage reported by the failing node.
This field may be empty if the failure message could not be decoded.

switchrpcForwardingFailure.description:
ForwardingFailure represents an HTLC failure that occurred at a remote node
in the payment route. The onion error was successfully decrypted, revealing
the failing hop.

switchrpcInFlight.description:
InFlight means the attempt has not resolved and its HTLC may be live. Keep
tracking it, and do not record a terminal outcome in the meantime.

switchrpcLocalFailure.description:
LocalFailure represents a failure that originates at the local node, as
reported by TrackOnion. SendOnion reports a local rejection through the
Rejected outcome instead, which carries the raw wire failure directly.

No onion decryption is involved because the failure occurred before the
HTLC left our node.

switchrpcNoRecord.description:
NoRecord means this server holds no record of the attempt_id.

It does NOT mean the attempt failed: a SendOnion for this attempt_id may
still be on its way. Resolve it by resending the original SendOnion request
with the same attempt_id, which either dispatches the attempt or answers
Accepted for the one already held. A caller that already received Accepted
for this attempt_id MUST NOT resend it, and should halt and alert instead,
because the record has been removed and the HTLC's outcome can no longer be
learned here.

This is a fact about the attempt rather than the call, and what it obliges
depends on what the caller already knows, so it is an answer and not a gRPC
error: as an error it would be the one exception to the rule that a gRPC
error means the call failed and should be retried. A server that never held
the attempt also answers NoRecord truthfully, so sending the track to the
server that accepted the attempt remains the caller's job.

wire_failure.description:
The BOLT #4 wire failure explaining the rejection, including any
channel update, as encoded by lnwire.EncodeFailure.

This is always present and always decodable. A rejection the switch
cannot describe is reported as Ambiguous instead, because a definite
verdict the caller cannot act on is worse than admitting uncertainty:
the caller has nothing to give its router and nothing to penalise with.

switchrpcRejected.description:
Rejected means the switch declined the HTLC before taking ownership of it.
The HTLC provably never left this node, so no funds are at risk and the
caller MAY fail this attempt and route elsewhere.

onion_blob.description: The raw onion packet to be sent across the network.

attempt_id.description:
The attempt ID uniquely identifying this payment attempt. The caller can
expect to track results for the payment via this attempt ID.

first_hop_pubkey.description:
The first hop's public key where the onion will be sent.
The first hop must be specified either by channel ID or public key.

first_hop_chan_id.description:
The channel id of the channel that must be taken to the first hop.
The first hop must be specified either by channel ID or public key.

amount.description:
The total amount in millisatoshis required to complete a payment over
this route. This value includes the cumulative fees at each hop. The HTLC
extended to the first-hop in the route will need to have at least this
many (milli)satoshis.

timelock.description:
The absolute timelock or CLTV value that should be extended to the first
hop in the route. All other hops will decrement the time-lock as
described by the onion.

payment_hash.description:
The payment hash associated with the HTLC. This is needed for tracking
and debugging purposes.

blinding_point.description:
The optional blinding point to use when constructing the HTLC.
If set, this will be used to blind the next hop in the route.

custom_records.description: Optional custom TLV records to include in the UpdateAddHTLC message.

extra_data.description: Optional opaque extra data to attach to the UpdateAddHTLC message.

switchrpcSendOnionResponse.description:
SendOnionResponse reports what the switch did with the attempt. Exactly one
outcome is always set.

A gRPC error from SendOnion means the call itself failed: a malformed
request, an auth failure, a transport problem, or a server not running this
sub-server. It never describes what happened to an HTLC. A caller that
receives an error and cannot distinguish those cases MUST retry the same
attempt_id, because a call that failed before reaching the server and a call
whose response was lost are indistinguishable from outside.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY, and this rule is load-bearing:

A caller that receives an outcome it does not recognise, or a response with
no outcome set at all, MUST treat it as Ambiguous and retry the same
attempt_id. It MUST NOT treat it as success, failure, or an empty response.

This matters because carrying the outcome in the response body trades one
safety property away and this rule buys it back. An unhandled gRPC error is
loud, while an unhandled response field is silent, so a caller built against
an older version of this service could otherwise misread a newer server's
answer as "nothing happened". Defaulting the unknown case to Ambiguous keeps
the failure mode a wasted retry rather than a lost or duplicated payment.

switchrpcSwitchError.description:
SwitchError indicates that the HTLC failed but its failure message could not
be encoded.

switchrpcTrackMode.description:
TrackMode selects how TrackOnion answers for an attempt that has not yet
resolved. A bounded wait may be added later as another value.

 - TRACK_MODE_WAIT: Wait until the attempt resolves, then answer with its result. A caller
that gives up on the wait should retry the same request. The switch
keeps an abandoned wait's subscription until the attempt resolves.
 - TRACK_MODE_PEEK: Answer at once, reporting an unresolved attempt as InFlight. A peek
only reads the attempt store and holds nothing on the server, so it is
the mode for callers that poll.

payment_hash.description:
The payment hash associated with the HTLC. This is needed for tracking
and debugging purposes.

attempt_id.description:
The attempt ID uniquely identifying this payment attempt. The caller can
expect to track results for the payment via this attempt ID.

session_key.description:
Optional: The session key that was used to construct the onion packet.
This is required by the server to decrypt any failure message.

hop_pubkeys.description:
Optional: The public keys of the nodes in the route, used with the
session_key to decrypt any failure message.

track_mode.description:
How to answer while the attempt has not resolved. The default waits for
it to resolve.

preimage.description:
The attempt settled, and this is its payment preimage. The caller
may record the payment as paid.

failure_details.description:
The attempt failed and its HTLC is no longer in flight. The caller
may fail the attempt and route elsewhere.

in_flight.description: The attempt has not resolved. Only returned for TRACK_MODE_PEEK.

no_record.description: This server holds no record of the attempt.

switchrpcTrackOnionResponse.description:
TrackOnionResponse reports what this server knows about the attempt. At most
one result is set.

A gRPC error from TrackOnion means the call itself failed: a malformed
request (InvalidArgument), an auth failure, a transport problem, a passed
deadline, an internal error, or a switch shutting down. It never describes
the attempt. The caller retries the same request, correcting it first if it
was malformed.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY, and this rule is load-bearing:

A caller that receives a result it does not recognise, or a response with
no result set at all, MUST treat the attempt as possibly still live and keep
tracking it. It MUST NOT treat the attempt as failed.

Reading "no preimage" as failure is the natural mistake here, and the
costly one: a caller that fails an attempt whose HTLC is still live and
routes another pays twice. The server also leaves the result unset when it
holds an answer it cannot describe, so this rule covers that case as well
as results added later.

switchrpcUnreadableFailure.description:
UnreadableFailure indicates that decryption keys were provided and
decryption was attempted, but failed. The original failure information
cannot be recovered.
